description: Live updates were rebuilt around hashes: the browser keeps the last data it received for each part of the app plus the server's hash, and asks only about the hashes it holds. The server compares them and answers in priority order - status, chat, dashboard, then the rest - with data only for what changed and a plain unchanged answer for the rest; nothing is pushed on connect, and an expired session now returns you to the sign-in page (a real 401) instead of retrying forever.
features: Live updates now load from the console's own cache: the browser keeps the last data it received for each part of the app together with the server's hash, and asks the server only about the hashes it holds, so nothing re-renders needlessly and the console paints instantly.

Answers arrive on the one existing connection in priority order - status first, then the agent chat, then the dashboard, then everything else (Workspace, scheduled tasks, gateway) - and only the parts that really changed carry data.
A part that did not change answers unchanged (no data sent, your stored copy stays), and no snapshot is pushed when the page connects any more.
An expired session now signs you out properly: the console returns to the sign-in page (a real 401) instead of reconnecting forever, while ordinary network blips still reconnect by themselves.

Fixed: live updates never reached the open console - the browser tab, the live view, chat progress, scheduled task states and the WhatsApp gateway were pushed into a second copy of the update module; one connection now serves every page.
Loading the console no longer creates a second copy of the shared UI module (two different cache versions were requested): modals, toasts and animations now always share one state.
The sign-in gate no longer hands your owner email to an unauthenticated visitor: the login page still learns whether an owner exists, while the email itself is returned only to a signed-in caller.

All embeddings (tool search, trigger search, chat memory, document search, semantic text memory) now live in one local ChromaDB vector database under X5Agent/Data/vector/chroma, still inside Data so a full backup/restore carries them.
Search history is no longer capped: chat memory search, the semantic text memory and document indexing keep growing instead of silently dropping the oldest 500 or 1000 entries.

Existing installs upgrade themselves: the old JSON vector files are imported into the new database automatically on first run, and tool/trigger search still starts instantly offline from the shipped seeds.

Tool/trigger indexing is unchanged from your side: editing a tool description still re-embeds only that tool (per-spec fingerprints), and a fresh copy needs no embedding call when the descriptions are unchanged.

Remote live browser view: the browser publishes one token-gated viewer port (8790 by default, X5_LIVE_VIEWER_PORT to change it) and the viewer link carries the session token, so the live page opens on your console address from any machine.

The raw relay port (6080) stays loopback-only: the gate serves the library's own viewer page, proxies the stream and the noVNC assets, forces the mode from the token (a preview link can never become interactive), and answers Not Connect (410) to anything without a live token.
The gate opens with the browser and closes with it, and the installer opens its port in the firewall next to the console port (best-effort, never fatal).
Starting the browser no longer shows a failed step when it is already running (uptime note kept); real refusals still fail clearly.
Refresh paints under the black splash: the splash lifts only after the cached data really landed (700ms floor, 2.5s ceiling), so chat and dashboard no longer pop in after the reveal.
The insecure-connection notice about the live view appears once per tab instead of on every refresh.
Tailscale/Funnel is gone: no tunnel, no registration link, no admin approval, no tailscale.json.
The console binds every interface on port 7777, so it opens directly at http://<your-ip>:7777/.
Setup is six steps instead of seven (the public-link step was removed) and the report shows the local and the reachable URL.
x5agent, install.py --run and Docker all serve on 0.0.0.0:7777; the public-link flags (--public/--no-public, X5_PUBLIC) are removed.
Remote live-browser view: the viewer link now points at your console host (open the viewer port to watch the browser from elsewhere).
Typing @ mid-word in Arabic opens the file picker; emails like mail@x never trigger it.
@file and /skill boundaries match between editor paint and server injection, including Arabic adjacency.
Browser downloads auto-move to Workspace/downloads; no empty folder hides the live view anymore.
Blue @file highlight keeps the same glyph widths as the text, so the caret no longer looks stuck inside a character.
The browser stays open: WSL idle-shutdown can no longer tear the live stack down mid-session.
Live downloads are bridged into the watched folder, so finished files always arrive in Workspace/downloads.
Files and folders inside downloads/ now show a delete button; the downloads folder itself can never be deleted.
Every model call (text, vision, STT, TTS, image) now routes AIP/1 records through the same interpreter path as the agent loop; legacy connections behave exactly as before.
Scheduled/trigger skill generation also falls back to the legacy engine for legacy-configured models, so task creation works with either record type.
Armed triggers keep working after a restart (watchers re-arm automatically).
Schedules accept seconds (every 30s) and invalid repeat patterns are rejected with a clear error.
Editing a scheduled task or trigger regenerates its skill so it never goes stale.
Library page triggers (manage_triggers) now create a Skill from the task plus the last-10 chat, arm the matching browser trigger, and run the Skill once when the page event fires.
One entry owns one library trigger plus one Skill: create one entry per event for a dedicated Skill each on the same site.
The library supports many concurrent triggers at once (up to 100; the project caps at 50) plus several OR events inside one trigger.
Trigger executions now run in their own hidden session instead of the main chat; the session is deleted with the trigger.
Scheduled run sessions render like the main chat: rich text, Working steps with elapsed time, and copy/edit/regenerate/delete on every message.
The task skill arrives as a normal user message and follow-ups show the same Working block and action bars as the main session.
Completed tasks no longer show a Pause button; only active or paused tasks can toggle it.
Executions list redesigned with status chips, run time, open arrow, and output previews; floating task cards restyled with status edge strips.
Task follow-ups are sent raw with the skill seeded once in the branch history and the full main-chat context, so the session answers like a separate normal chat instead of repeating the task reply.
Execution context is now guaranteed: system prompt + memories + environment + skill-as-message + same tools, never chat history.
The main context lists every armed trigger with its task and how to manage it.
Scheduled run pages no longer show the task name on top, so they fit phones.
Opening a scheduled run auto-hides the floating Scheduled Tasks window.
Settings has a black Delete chat history button with the live message count and a loading spinner; it clears the main chat + its search index only — saved memories stay.

New pdf_create tool behind tool_search: create a whole slide deck from one slides JSON (create), edit it later by task_id with only changed slides regenerating (update), or fetch the stored JSON plus the latest PDF (get).

Missing-model tools no longer stop the loop: the tool is skipped with its connect message, the model decides to continue or present it, and the final reply carries a Connect button for the right AI Models dialog.
Every model call now sends the seed context plus the last 30 conversation units (one reply or one call+output each), keeping linkage without unbounded history.
Unconnected tools now end the reply with a per-tool Connect/Skip choice (no note message): Skip sends the agent a message to continue without the tool, Connect opens that tool's AI Models dialog.
PDF decks arrive as a designed file card under the reply: click opens a preview with per-image downloads plus whole-file download.
PDF decks support page sizes (A4/Letter/square, rectangle default) and render through headless Chrome so the PDF matches the slide design exactly, with a pure-Python fallback when Chrome is missing.
PDF rendering rebuilt for true fidelity: each slide file prints separately with its full design and the pages merge into one PDF (selectable text, embedded images, exact page size).
The PDF file card is redesigned with page info and a full-screen preview with per-image downloads plus whole-file download.
Missing-model tools pause with a Connect/Skip strip above the composer (both continue without the tool; Connect also opens that model's dialog).
Attached images are injected exactly where mentioned, render centered in the message, and Workspace files carry stable ids everywhere.
The PDF builder sees the same tool catalog and Workspace map as the main agent and resolves image and file ids into the deck folder automatically.
Project card in Settings redesigned with a cleaner repository + version layout.
Update check fixed: the description is back within its 500-char limit and the console version matches updates.json.
Default white buttons (Cancel / secondary actions) are now professional glass, matching the dashboard glass language; black and red buttons keep their look.
White buttons redesigned as light ovals (Change password, Delete chat history, Cancel): solid pill, dark text, gentle lift on hover.
Public link stays alive: the live stream survives Tailscale Funnel resets (proxy-safe SSE headers + 15s heartbeat) instead of dying with 502.
No more false logout over the public link: the page goes to login only when the session is proven expired, otherwise it reconnects by itself.
Reconnects fast after a funnel blip (1s/2s/5s backoff) and replays the latest snapshot on every redial.
Black boot splash with the Working ring-wave dots and wave brand text replaces all skeleton shimmer templates, including the agent chat placeholders.
The splash lifts only after all boot data is ready (live snapshot plus dashboard, charts, chat, plugins, skills, models, workspace, scheduler, gateway and settings first loads).
Page entrance replays on reveal, and a 15s watchdog guarantees the splash can never trap the screen when the backend is unreachable.
Balance card shows measured lifetime spend (per-request captured prices summed), e.g. $0.55 measured spend · 174 requests, instead of the empty connect-a-model state.
Daily cost charts use the same per-request sums, so charts and Balance always agree; older rows without a capture are priced from the cached table.
Boot splash never flashes on fast loads: it only appears when loading takes longer than a moment, otherwise the screen goes straight to data.
Boot reveal is a single animation: page content stays hidden until all data lands, then appears exactly once with its entrance - no multi-jump refresh.
Balance pricing also matches short custom model names to provider rates (gpt-4o-mini finds openai/gpt-4o-mini), so more requests measure a real dollar cost.
The setup one-liner and x5agent now start the console detached: safe to close SSH, same command restarts (old server killed, new one on 7777).
x5agent --off (alias x5agent-off) stops every project server on the port.
Server log lives in X5Agent/Data/logs/console.log for persistent runs.
Every Workspace file owns one stable id (its Workspace-relative path) shown in the context map, the @ picker, and @ mention lines, so the agent compares ids instead of guessing names.
Chat uploads mirror into Workspace under their original name (suffixed only on collision) and arrive as image metadata plus a priority Workspace pointer in the same request.
@ picks render blue in the sent bubble and regenerate/edit resends inject the identical @ ids and / skill.
vision_analyze resolves Workspace file ids directly (jailed), and pdf_create accepts folder file ids, copies them jailed into the deck, and tells the slide session to use the exact id as .
Connect always reaches the AI Models dialog even when its pause already expired, and no pause strip ever appears after STOP.

Every file line (Workspace map, uploads, folder listings) carries id + full path + type + size; @ mentions send @<file-id> + full path in place (the map holds the rest) while the picked name stays blue in the message.
The Workspace map instructs the agent to use exact path links and to copy any file into its working folder so everything lives in one folder.
pdf_create accepts Workspace-relative sub-path file ids (jailed, traversal rejected) and copies them into the deck preserving the relative path the slide HTML references.
WhatsApp/Telegram uploads use the same unified file logic: original-name Workspace mirror plus full id/path/type/size hints with analyze/search pointers.
Terminal steps now show a fixed Terminal Command title; the full command plus exit code and output tail live under the arrow.
PDF builds narrate each finished slide in Arabic under the arrow (finished slide N) plus a final line merging all slides into the PDF.
pdf_create ships two bundled default fonts (Amiri for Arabic, Cairo for Latin) applied automatically when the user uploads no font.

A tool that needs an unconnected model keeps its strip above the composer (refresh-safe, STOP drops it): Connect opens the model dialog and reruns the same tool once saved, Skip continues with an Arabic skip note to the model.
File and folder paths the model writes in chat replies now render blue: one click opens the Workspace page with that file revealed at its path.

Stopping mid-task turns the send button into a plain oval white Continue pill (black text, no glow; empty composer only, animated pop-in, refresh-safe): tapping it resumes the stopped task in place with no new bubble, and typing anything flips it back to normal send as a brand-new request.
Resuming a stopped task removes its Stopped divider (live and after refresh) while every step stays, so the continuation lands right after the previous steps.
Continue resumes inside the SAME Working block: the frozen block wakes (wave restarts) and new steps append to its existing step list instead of opening a new bubble.

STOP is real from the first press: model requests abort mid-read, retry backoff is interruptible, provider errors break at once on cancel, and the wait tool stops immediately — the frozen Working steps always stay visible.
Stopping and continuing repeatedly never stacks Stopped dividers: a re-stop refreshes the same marker in place.

The send button is state-aware: with an empty composer and no task it is a disabled normal send (question choices still send normally); deleting the whole chat disarms Continue; editing a message forces normal send.

Continue is now seamless: no internal message appears in the UI or in the agent's context (no L8, no stopped note on resume) — the model continues as if the task never stopped, while a new message after a stop still tells it the task was stopped.

New svg_maker tool behind tool_search: describe the wanted icon and it returns raw SVG code only plus the saved .svg file in Workspace (same text model, dedicated icon session, validated and sanitized).

pdf_studio is now the only way to create a PDF: it prepares a numbered studio (Data/studios/pdf_N with studio.json + pages/PageNN.jsx + assets/fonts + assets/images) and ends with an Open Studio card.

New fullscreen studio route /studio-pdf/<id> above the agent template: fixed toolbar, white A4 page in the middle, floating unified agent composer, auto-created pages, black-screen working lights, hot-reload on approve.
New studio_approve core tool: delivers the complete React code for one page, trial-builds it, and hot-reloads on success (must be called before the task counts as done).
New studio_read_slide core tool: number-only read of another slide, empty when that slide is still blank.

New pdf_studio_system.md studio prompt (English): all tools stay available, slide states plus studio files listed twice plus full Workspace plus user question drive the loop, multi-page delivery in one session.
Main prompts now route any PDF/slide request to pdf_studio with an Open Studio card.
Studio shell is built once in project/web/studio-pdf (React) and every studio backup is zipping X5Agent/Data/studios.
Studio names are unique: creating or renaming with a used name fails clearly so the agent asks for another name (each studio keeps its own separate session).
pdf_studio renames via the SAME tool (action=rename) and no longer takes page counts — it only creates the project, the studio grows pages itself.
Studio shell is the exact PDF Maker design (toolbar, feed, zoom, floating composer) built once to dist; the MIME failure is fixed (real JS MIME, assets 404 instead of HTML).
Studio opens with an animation on its session route (/studio-pdf/<id>, Back closes, deep-link opens it) and the reply ends with a rectangle card with a glass OPEN button.
Studios are never deleted by anything now: not by regenerate/edit/prune, and not by Delete-chat-history either (it clears the main chat + search index only).
Approved page code runs live in the white page with hot-reload (one code per slide file); render errors never reach the user — they go back to the agent silently for the next fix.

Studio context now carries every slide (number + state + place), the current-page task micro-prompt, the 2 studio tools first, the unified 794x1123 page size, studio assets twice, Workspace and request uploads.
Studio toolbar is export (animated 0-100 like pdf-motion) + previous/next + portrait/landscape toggle only; overlay closes with animation; the in-studio composer matches the main agent template.
Studio toolbar undo/redo steps through every delivered state of the current page (each approve is saved, nothing is lost).

Each slide owns its loading state: sending from one page shows its loader above the composer while other pages stay normal and sendable; orientation locks on the first prompt; zoom has an explicit reset.
A deleted studio opens a friendly missing screen (no more 404 poll spam) with one tap back to the chat.
The in-studio composer is now the exact main-agent template (attachments, Studio mode pill, grouped send).
A new studio starts with ONE page only — scrolling down inside adds each next page as a real empty file, one by one.
The studio card at the end of the reply is redesigned: glowing mark, studio name, live page count and a glass OPEN button.
Studio turns now run the real isolated agent loop (approves land on their own; the shell request only carries the white animation plus the send-mark loader).
Studio attach menu holds images + font files only, uploaded for real into studio assets (type and content validated).
Studio voice mirrors the main agent: missing speech model routes to the AI Models template, otherwise the recording template with live bars, timer and direct send.
The sent request is never shown: only the white-page animation plus a locking loader on the send mark (typing more text cannot send while its slide designs).
Studio UI state persists per studio (page, zoom, orientation, draft, lock) and entry shows a black preparing screen until all data is ready — everything real, no simulation.
Fixed the dead studio turn (wrong loop name crashed every design silently) — turns now execute for real and failures toast their reason instead of vanishing.
The designing black screen now fills the whole page, and the send mark locks unmistakably (dimmed + spinner, no re-send) while its slide designs.
Studio turns never touch the main chat or session anymore (fixed the leak) and run on a minimal sentence+state context with a hard 25-step cap — no more 60k-token wandering.
The three session tools are now ONE studio_page tool (list / read / deliver / patch): every write is auto-tested with the result returned as output, and writes work only on the tasked slide.
Full-code delivery fixed: the dispatcher 10k args cap no longer rejects page designs, and the silently-crashing slide-states context (missing variable) is fixed — designs can actually land now.
The studio send button becomes a red STOP while a turn runs (halts the loop entirely); stopped or empty turns offer a Continue pill that resumes the last request (refresh-safe, like the main agent).
Re-entering a studio shows the black loading template from the server designing flag — never a blank reset; a turn that ends with no design frees the mark honestly.
The outer studio card shows a live status dot (orange pulsing while generating, green when all pages are designed) with the actual page count, and clicking anywhere on it opens the studio.
The studio entry toast is removed.

One box per studio (pdf-motion preset method): portrait 794x1123 or landscape 1123x794 stored server-side — the preview, the model context and the export all read the same size, so mismatch is impossible; switching freezes after the first request.
The studio prompt now teaches the exact pdf-motion page method (locked min/max box, margins, doc type scale, children wrapper, no flex spreading, bidi numbers).
The live renderer forces classic JSX and shims react/jsx-runtime, so delivered designs can no longer blank the page on a missing runtime.
STOP now plays a stopping animation until the loop actually halts (plus the pending-cancel race fix).
The black loading template is translucent: the current design shows through while the next one generates.
A broken compile or render falls back to the last good design instead of a blank page (the error still reaches the agent silently for auto-fix).
PDF export renders at pixelRatio 3 (max quality), skips a broken page with a count instead of failing the whole file, and the Google Fonts cssRules SecurityError is fixed via crossorigin.
Every new studio reply ends with the Open Studio card plus the studio link line, so the agent knows the link and WhatsApp/Telegram chats receive it as plain text (no button needed).
The black entry loading screen is removed: the studio opens instantly on the white page and approved designs stream in as they arrive.
Undo/redo buttons work now (the studio API returns history counts, so they enable correctly) with slide animations — back slides from the left, forward from the right.
Scrolling is smoother on desktop (softer glide, snappier page flips, trackpad micro-scroll stays native) and on phones (lighter swipe, jank-free pinch zoom with animated zoom transitions).
The toolbar shows the studio title with an ellipsis plus a page-count pill (1 / 3) instead of one cramped string.

Studio sessions now run exactly 3 tools: studio_page approves the tasked slide (read/deliver/patch/test on its file only, every write auto-tested with errors kept silent from the user), studio_read views any other slide read-only, and http_request GETs/POSTs links (no tool_search in studio).

Parallel studio turns per slide on the same branch session: one slide runs at most one turn (a second request on the same slide is refused with a clear message), while different slides design in parallel; STOP and Continue are per-page.
Slide white halo fixed: the studio frame and live page fill are transparent and follow the design background, so no white edges grow around slides when zooming.

Uploaded studio images and fonts now render live inside the page: a new /api/studio/asset route serves them with real MIME (path-validated, canvas-safe), and the context lists every asset with its exact src path for and @font-face (uploads appear twice: assets block plus the request section).

Studio designer now follows a professional bar (hero element, hierarchy, cohesive tokens, zero placeholders), always reviews the previous slide for deck consistency, picks the palette from the content when the user did not specify one, and fetches photos and fonts from a verified in-prompt sources catalog (Openverse, Wikimedia, Cleveland CC0, pet APIs, Fontsource, Google, Bunny, Fontshare) with uploads first and 3 fetches max per page.

Web images and fonts the design uses now save into the studio assets automatically (offline/export-safe, hotlink kept on failure): deliberate saves carry the search words as the asset description, and the context shows every asset with what it is.
Vision tool appears in studio sessions only while a vision model is connected, and it can inspect studio images directly (studio:pdf_N/images/name).

Toolbar delete-slide button: blank slides delete at once, designed slides ask with a cannot-be-undone confirm, later slides shift up; locked while anything generates. Undo/redo is a single flicker-free slide and locks during generation.
Phone toolbar collapses into a ⋯ menu with every option; opening the studio lands directly on the last page with no entry glide, and rotating to phone mode holds the current page.
Studio shows an offline notice after repeated unreachable polls instead of stale spinners, failed sends hand the text back to the composer, and refreshing inside a studio keeps the session open.
Gateway studio links prefer the live public URL and rewrite dead loopback links, so WhatsApp/Telegram links actually open when the public link is on.
Edit turns now carry the tasked slide's current code directly in context (no read round-trip); other slides stay states-only and old versions never travel.
Undo/redo is now a pure fade (out then in, no sliding, no flicker), step buttons lock during generation, and failed sends hand the text back to the composer.
Phone ⋯ is a horizontal icon strip under the toolbar (export/undo/redo/orientation/zoom-reset/delete) with in/out animation; the + attach menu matches the main template and closes on outside tap.
Refreshing inside a studio keeps it open on the same page, deleted studios never open (dead cards swept), and deleting the last slide lands on an existing one without auto-creating.
Vision appears in studio sessions only while a vision model is connected and is never mentioned in the system prompt.
Scrolling inside the studio never creates pages anymore: a fixed white + button in the toolbar (phone and desktop) is the only page creator — one press adds the page and scrolls to it.
Phone ⋯ menu is now a floating rounded card with rise+scale show/hide animations (outside tap closes it with the same exit animation).

The studio card at the end of the reply is redesigned: whole-card glass button with an arrow (no OPEN button, keyboard-openable), English status line, designed/pending counts, and a status dot — orange while generating, green for unseen designs, grey when all caught up.
New studio cards rise in with a professional appear animation and the chat pins fully to the bottom with room for the card; opening the chat lands at the very bottom too.
The toolbar + is now a white icon with no background (same language as the other toolbar icons).
On phones the prev/next arrows live inside the ⋯ menu (PDF export stays toolbar-only); the toolbar keeps PDF, +, size and zoom so it fits without scrolling.
Cancelling a PDF export is instant now: the progress overlay hides at once and the running render loop is superseded so no file dialog pops up late.
The reply-end studio card is a slim rectangle in the exact dashboard glass system with a background-less arrow at the end and ultra-clean title/status/counts hierarchy.
New AI Models template AI Vision Videos (videos-only, own setup prompt): connect video-understanding endpoints separately from the still-images Vision model.
video_analyze now sends the video itself to the Vision Videos template only (oversize clips are shrunk with ffmpeg to fit one request); vision_analyze stays still-images only.

Fixed pasted-parser failures (e.g. position 1011): the text/vision setup examples carried an extra brace that assistants copied verbatim — all six example parsers are strict-valid JSON now and locked by test.

New image_search tool behind tool_search: send search words and it returns ready-to-use picture metadata (searched text, width/height, mime, byte size, source, title/credit, Workspace file path) with verified copies saved into Workspace/images/ — fans out to Openverse, Wikimedia, Flickr, Internet Archive, NASA, Cleveland, Art Institute of Chicago, Iconify SVG, pet/food/pokemon APIs plus a Picsum fallback, search-only with no keys.

Studio photo flow now runs on image_search: the manual http_request image catalog is removed from the studio prompt (fonts/links stay on http_request), studio sessions carry 4 tools, and studio_page fetch accepts an image_search Workspace file (copied into studio assets with the search words as its description, no re-download).

image_search is now two-homed: studio turns pass studio_id and pictures land straight in that studio's assets as src paths (the whole studio context is Workspace-free and self-contained; the engine strips studio_id in the main chat so it can never write studio assets), while the main agent keeps Workspace/images/ files that now render as the normal end-of-reply image card with fullscreen zoom.
New generate_image tool behind tool_search: describe the picture and it draws via the connected AI Image Model, saving into X5Agent/Data/files/images.

Every image tool shares one end-of-reply card template: centered half-width professional card (screenshots + generated), keyboard-openable, fullscreen viewer with buttons + wheel + drag + double-tap zoom.
New /api/image route serves generated images path-validated (png/jpg/webp/gif, 8MB cap) with the same bounded final_images pipeline (dedupe, traversal-reject, max 6).
Chat regenerate/edit/prune never touch studios — and neither does Delete-chat-history anymore.

Settings has Backup & Restore: Backup now downloads every client data (chat, PDF Studios, memories, skills, files, settings and API keys) as one .zip file with a loading bar; system code and the embedding model are never included.
Restore picks a backup .zip of any size, asks for confirmation, uploads it with a progress bar and replaces ALL client data from the backup (you may need to sign in again afterwards).
Agent context now lists Available PDF Studios (one short line each: id, name, page count, designed count) so the agent reuses instead of duplicating.
pdf_studio tool reopens an existing studio via action=open + studio_id (nothing created); create is only for when every studio already has designs.
Mission rule: an empty (0 designed) studio is handed back first; a brand-new studio is created only when all are designed or the user explicitly asks for new.

pdf_studio create accepts pages (up to 10 descriptions, one per slide): the studio is created at once and every design starts in parallel in the background — the user opens it and finds them generating, per-page STOP included.

Mission rule: when the user says what is inside the PDF, the agent writes the page prompts itself and sends them with creation; without specified content it creates the empty studio and lets the user drive.
Studio entry has no full-space cover anymore: every slide shows its own in-box loading lights with the same animation and a Loading word until its design lands.
Reply-end studio card restyled: slimmer glass card with fully rounded corners in the dashboard glass language.
Entering a studio shows Loading lights inside every page box for 2s, then fades automatically — even when the designs are already there.
Phone toolbar: the square mark is hidden and every icon (PDF, +, trash, size, zoom, more) sits on the left with title and count alone on the right.
Reply-end studio card redesigned as a thin Gateway-style row card: glass document tile, title row with status dot, status line, counts line and chevron — keyboard-openable native button.
In-studio composer placeholder is now Describe your design, or paste your content...
Cached studio pages run direct: no loading overlay ever covers a loaded design — lights show only while its turn generates, with bigger dots and word.
Phone toolbar fixed: square mark hidden, orientation toggle out of the toolbar (still inside the more menu), every icon left with title and count right — the 3-dots button always visible.
Reply-end studio card no longer prints All caught up: quiet studios show title plus counts only.
Loaded studio designs never flash loading: the box stays blank until the design streams in, lights only while its turn generates.
Reply-end card status always pairs text with its dot: Generating, new-designs, or Ready for quiet studios — no All caught up line.
Phone toolbar keeps exactly 4 icons left (PDF, add, zoom-reset, more); trash, orientation and zoom in/out live only inside the more menu.

pdf_studio is now the single place to see studios too: action=list shows every studio with its state (pages, designed, orientation, live designing), action=get shows one studio's full details (slide states, assets).
Agent context no longer auto-lists studios — one fixed pointer line tells the model to call action=list first, so reuse-before-create still holds with a smaller, always-fresh context.
The Plugins page is gone from the console: no sidebar entry, no route, no boot wait — the sidebar goes Dashboard, Agent, Workspace, Gateway, Skills, AI Models, Settings.
Tool search seeds rebuilt (57 tools, hash 383b8571) so fresh installs find tools instantly with zero model calls.
Browser engine updated from x5browser 1.5.2 to 1.6.0.
Sign-in popups (Google/Firebase) now survive, so logins finish instead of the window closing early.
Closing the browser really closes it: Chrome is asked to quit and the debug endpoint is verified gone, so the next open starts a fresh browser.
A refused browser command no longer starts Chrome (and no longer leaks a stray Chrome process holding the debug port).
Closing the active tab returns a clean result instead of an error.
The browser launcher refuses to attach to a Chrome running on someone else's profile.
The agent's browser tool set is unchanged: the library's new image_search tool is not exposed, the project's own image_search plugin keeps that name and behavior.
Browser engine updated to x5browser 1.6.1.
Fixed on WSL/Linux: the library attaches to its own Chrome again — 1.6.0's ownership check wrongly refused the unit-driven browser inside the distro as a foreign endpoint (port_in_use).
The launcher's command-line check is stricter: a profile named like ours (…-profile-old) or a longer port (92230 vs 9223) is no longer mistaken for our browser.
The agent's browser tool set is unchanged (no tools added or removed in 1.6.1).

Tailscale registration no longer fails when its link expires: a fresh link is issued automatically while you register (up to 3 attempts), so setup never has to be re-run just because you were slow to open it.
Tailscale registration output is a single clean box with the link shown once; the noisy raw lines and the redundant 'no browser on this server' note are gone.
The memory system is now exactly four memories: your profile (who you are), the agent's personality, confirmed facts about you, and the agent's own private notes.
The agent personality memory is sent to the agent every request as its identity, so over time it learns your style, taste and way of working and becomes a copy of you.
New memory tool: the agent can read, write, edit or delete its own long-term notes by itself — the only memory it controls, and it is never sent automatically.
Facts memory absorbed the old important-notes memory, and the separate image memory is gone (images are ordinary Workspace files now).
Long-term memories are refreshed every 30 messages (was 50) and any memory that passes 1000 tokens is compressed automatically without losing information.
Old memories are kept: existing user and agent memory files are read and upgraded in place, so nothing is lost.
